s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic unilateral eyelid swelling with purulent discharge
salient_findings: 2-year history of swelling of the right upper eyelid
Pus discharge for 10 months without trauma
Immovable scarlike node on the right upper eyelid
Ring enhancement in the right frontal sinus on MRI
Opacification of the right frontal, ethmoid, and maxillary sinuses on CT
key_facts: 52-year-old Japanese woman
2-year history of right upper eyelid swelling
10 months of pus discharge
No history of trauma to the head
No symptoms of fever, headache, or nasal discharge
Immovable scarlike node on the right upper eyelid
Node measures 11 × 7 mm
MRI shows high signal on T2-weighted image and ring enhancement in the right frontal sinus
CT shows opacification of the right frontal, ethmoid, and maxillary sinuses
Expansion of the right frontal and ethmoid sinuses without bone destruction
Histopathology reveals mild inflammatory infiltrate with fibrosis and lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate

shortlist.label: Chronic dacryocystitis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic unilateral eyelid swelling with purulent discharge, consistent with blockage of the nasolacrimal duct

shortlist.label: Frontal sinus mucocele
shortlist.why_kept: Imaging studies show opacification and expansion of the right frontal sinus, consistent with a mucocele

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic angiocentric fibrosis
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathology reveals mild inflammatory infiltrate with fibrosis and lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate, and the presence of eosinophils

shortlist.label: Kimura disease
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of chronic eyelid swelling and histopathological findings of lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate and eosinophils

shortlist.label: Churg-Strauss syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of eosinophils and history of chronic sinusitis, although less likely given the lack of systemic symptoms

raw.rationale: The presence of an immovable scarlike node on the eyelid with chronic pus discharge, along with histopathological findings of mild inflammatory infiltrate, fibrosis, and lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate, and the absence of systemic symptoms or bone destruction, are consistent with eosinophilic angiocentric fibrosis, a rare condition characterized by chronic inflammation and fibrosis of the affected tissue.

rejected.label: Chronic dacryocystitis
rejected.why: Lack of symptoms related to the lacrimal gland or duct, such as epiphora or dacryolithiasis

rejected.label: Frontal sinus mucocele
rejected.why: Absence of significant bone destruction or expansion that would typically be seen with a mucocele

rejected.label: Kimura disease
rejected.why: Typically presents with lymphadenopathy and eosinophilia, which are not mentioned in the case

rejected.label: Churg-Strauss syndrome
rejected.why: Characterized by asthma, eosinophilia, and vasculitis, which are not present in this case
